title: CV Tutorial chapters 16–20 evidence ledger
scope: Historical architecture claims checked against primary papers and official operator documentation; code and diagram calculations are illustrative, not benchmark reproductions.

entries.claim: R-CNN uses around 2000 category-independent Selective Search proposals, warps each region to 227x227 and extracts 4096-D CNN features before class-specific linear SVM scoring
entries.notes: Paper-specific AlexNet/Caffe configuration; proposal count is approximate, not a universal constant.

entries.claim: R-CNN trains a separate linear bounding-box regressor from proposal features to reduce localization errors
entries.notes: The main paper points to supplementary material for detailed regression parameterization; article labels the shown encoding as a standard relative-box parameterization.

entries.claim: Selective Search hierarchically merges adjacent superpixels using low-level region similarities
entries.locator: Uijlings et al., Selective Search for Object Recognition
entries.notes: It is an external, non-end-to-end proposal algorithm, not a learned R-CNN head.

entries.claim: Fast R-CNN computes a shared feature map, applies RoI Pooling to fixed HxW features, then uses K+1 classification and K class-specific box-regression outputs
entries.notes: The paper gives 7x7 as an example for VGG16; background class has no box target.

entries.claim: Fast R-CNN multi-task loss combines classification log loss and foreground-gated Smooth L1 box loss
entries.notes: Toy code verifies gradient gating; it is not a full training reproduction.

entries.claim: RoIAlign removes RoI Pooling coordinate quantization for accurate mask alignment
entries.notes: RoIAlign is a Mask R-CNN-era extension, not the original Fast R-CNN layer.

entries.claim: Original Faster R-CNN uses 3 scales and 3 aspect ratios, yielding 9 anchors per feature-map location
entries.notes: Paper example uses areas 128², 256², 512² and aspect ratios 1:1, 1:2, 2:1.

entries.claim: RPN positive anchors are highest-IoU per ground truth or IoU>0.7; negatives have IoU<0.3 to all GT; others ignored
entries.notes: Paper samples 256 anchors per image with positive:negative ratio up to 1:1; cross-boundary anchors are ignored in training.

entries.claim: Faster R-CNN paper experiments use four-step alternating training; approximate joint training is discussed separately
entries.notes: Do not conflate the paper's experiment protocol with later common implementations.

entries.claim: YOLOv1 VOC configuration uses S=7, B=2, C=20 and output tensor 7x7x30; class probabilities are shared per cell
entries.notes: This describes YOLOv1, not the anchor-based multi-scale output of later YOLO generations.

entries.claim: YOLOv1 confidence equals object probability times IoU; class-specific score multiplies cell conditional class probability by confidence
entries.notes: YOLOv1 uses one class-probability vector per grid cell, not one per predicted box.

entries.claim: Original SSD300 uses six prediction feature maps and 8732 default boxes
entries.notes: Counts 38²×4 + 19²×6 + 10²×6 + 5²×6 + 3²×4 + 1²×4. Other SSD input sizes/configurations differ.

entries.claim: SSD matching first assigns best-overlap default box then all boxes with IoU>0.5; hard-negative mining caps negatives at 3:1
entries.locator: Section 2.2, Matching strategy and Hard negative mining
entries.notes: The 3:1 ratio is the paper's training procedure, not a universal property of all one-stage detectors.

entries.claim: Original U-Net uses valid 3x3 convolutions, 572x572 input and 388x388 output, with 23 convolutional layers
entries.notes: Modern same-padding U-Net implementations can preserve spatial dimensions and differ from the original geometry.

entries.claim: Each decoder stage upsamples, crops the corresponding encoder feature map, concatenates channels and applies two valid convolutions
entries.notes: This is concatenation, not residual elementwise addition.

entries.claim: Original U-Net uses weighted pixel-wise softmax cross entropy with a weight map emphasizing touching-cell borders
entries.notes: Dice loss is a later common objective; the article does not attribute it to the original U-Net paper.

entries.claim: Original U-Net uses overlap-tile inference with mirrored context at image borders and elastic deformation augmentation
entries.notes: The tiling method uses a larger input context and predicts a smaller valid central region.

entries.claim: RetinaNet combines a feature pyramid with dense classification and box regression subnetworks; Focal Loss modulates cross-entropy using alpha_t and gamma.
entries.notes: The article's curve and scalar code are formula demonstrations, not benchmark measurements.

entries.claim: Original DETR uses a CNN backbone, Transformer encoder-decoder, learned object queries and Hungarian bipartite matching to train a fixed-size prediction set.
entries.notes: Original DETR avoids hand-designed anchors and NMS, but has slower convergence and weaker small-object performance; Deformable DETR is a later variant.
